protocol.name: meter-first full-store rho, 1024 workers, every visited class recorded
protocol.dpbits_note: v23 shipped one record per 2^100-step trail; the merge-stay law measured here makes any spacing > 1 step unable to convert a coalescence into a record match, so v24 ships one record per VISITED CLASS and the required stay-merge horizon is 1 step.
protocol.meter: one global counter in instructions; every action charges it; the worker asks before acting and abandons. Ledger closes at sum(rows) == W with W exact (no residual row).

row_derivations.walk_steps: steps x STEP; STEP = f_mul x MUL_CHARGE + (1-f_mul) x SQR_CHARGE, f_mul = measured 0.6364326388888889 from scan24.json:multiply/steps
row_derivations.per_step_lookup: steps x LOOKUP; LOOKUP = 96 Ir = 5 limb-mults (20) + 2 probes (32) + 2x64-bit compare (8) + hash tail (36): counted row in scripts/ir24/lookup_count.c
row_derivations.record_writes: steps x 64 Ir (key 6 words + A + D words, 8 stores of 8 B)
row_derivations.table_build_R65536: Rg x ENTRY_IR; ENTRY_IR = 2 x 383 dense muls (two 255-bit exponentiations g^a, z^b) at 20000
row_derivations.worker_starts_1024: 1024 x 383 dense muls (one 2-scalar start per worker)
row_derivations.candidate_verification: 1200 dense Fp12 muls (pairing) + one G1 scalar action

trap.model: waste = rate x E[delay] x STEP. Admission alone is not waste: the delay is the measured number of steps from admission to the stall-abort (32 consecutive squarings), control arm Rg=4096 depth=1 where the family admits.

success.bridge: P(solve) = CP95(census at the shipped shape) x P(stay merged for the record horizon). The horizon is 1 step because every visited class is recorded, so the second factor is MEASURED at exactly that gap (0.995 at Rg=65536), not extrapolated. rho^(production gap) is NOT used: the fitted rho=0.999323 with band 1.358 holds only for gaps <= 1000 (survival 0.4875 at gap 1000), and any protocol whose record horizon exceeded that band would have to multiply by a collapsing factor. That is the v23 defect, stated here as the reason dpbits=0 ships.

fidelity_table.status: DEVIATES (enumeration; the two scales differ so scaling is tested across groups, not resources)
DEVIATES: worker count only splits the same step budget; both self- and cross-worker collisions solve

DEVIATES: the table cost is group-size-independent (2^40 Ir), which is 2^99x the whole fixture budget; charging it at face value would make the fixture a measurement of the table build. The ledger charges it in full.

fidelity_table.fixture: charged in the ledger, not in the meter
fidelity_table.status: DEVIATES: 40x the fixture budget, 2^-100 of production W

peak_memory.statement: peak = records x 64 B + Rg x 96 B + 1024 x 256 B + 1024 x depth x 8 B + code, summed at protocol peak. This is the time-memory tradeoff: with w records the required step count is N/w, so 2^133 B is the price of the 2^126.0-step schedule; a 2^46 B pool (2^40 records) needs 2^211.3 steps. Memory is unscored but stated.
